heading: Meridian architecture overview
body: Meridian splits into three services: the scheduler, the capacity model, and the depot gateway. The gateway is the only component that talks to Corbel, which keeps the migration surface small.
author: p.osei

heading: Migration tool known issues
body: Recurring Corbel schedules with per-depot overrides do not survive migration. Workaround is to re-enter them by hand after import. Tracked as MIG-88.
author: r.vance

heading: Pricing working group notes, May
body: Three tiers still on the table. The group could not agree between a per-seat and a per-depot model. Finance wants a number above the Corbel list price. Nothing is approved.
author: j.mbeki

heading: Launch readiness checklist
body: Blockers before general availability: migration tool sign-off, depot gateway load test, support runbook, and a final pricing decision. Two of four are outstanding.
author: s.arden

heading: Support runbook draft
body: Escalation path for Meridian incidents. Note the seat entitlement check: customers on the $4,900 per seat plan get the two-hour response SLA.
author: s.arden

heading: General availability comms plan
body: Press embargo lifts the morning of October 14. Analyst briefings the day before, customer emails at 09:00 local.
author: l.ferreira

heading: Final pricing approved
body: Approved: $4,900 per seat per year on an annual commitment, volume breaks above 500 seats. Per-depot pricing is dropped.
author: j.mbeki

heading: Go-live plan for October 14
body: Cutover window opens 02:00 UTC on October 14. Rollback deadline is 06:00. Depot gateway stays on the old path for the first week.
author: s.arden

heading: Ferrous Labs integration plan
body: Post-acquisition, Meridian keeps its own roadmap through the next fiscal year. Ferrous Labs will fold the depot gateway into its own logistics stack after that.
author: p.osei

heading: Q4 retro
body: 1,240 seats in week one against a 900 seat target. Migration tool complaints dominated support volume, as expected.
author: r.vance
